observations: The noun paṇya identifies a thing offered for purchase and has a separate yat nipātana in the transactional sense of 01.0507.
Tat selects the named nominative merchandise, while asya gives a genitive possessor meaning. The derivative already includes the merchandise condition.
The three named food lines have independently written apūpa, śaṣkulī and modaka selections.
Ṭhañ takes the whole salt-merchant relation. Its ñ gives initial accent while the independent mixing role remains elsewhere.
The Kāśikā names nine aromatic bases and directly prints its first two masculine/feminine forms.
Most displays and the explicit feminine have narad-. The niradika display of one text layer is a flagged reading.
The two forms kiśara and kisara are positively paired in Vasu. Kaumudī gives both gendered derivatives with dental s.
Vasu additionally lists sthāgala, haridru and parṇī at the same source member relation.
The naming of scents can select material in which the particular scent is present, while this is still a sale-address.
For the final-u operands the expressed affix begins with k, retaining the root-side u.
Ṣ-it provides the feminine ṅīṣ pathway and the source gives explicit feminine ī pitch.
The two śalālu paths yield the same suffix sound by 7.3.51, and distinct gender markers produce the two long-ī results.
The nasal teaching markers in ṭhañ and ṣṭhan each have initial-accent consequences without automatically sharing the same vowel grade.
Vasu's four śalālu example marks distinguish initial masculine accent with ṣṭhan and final masculine accent with ṭhak, and final ī in both feminine displays.
The default, exception and option are conditioned by the actual merchandise word and its specified material.
decisions: Admit the three named food traders in the source case relation. Ordinary possession alone does not meet its merchandise condition.
Form the salt-trader stem with ṭhañ and keep its accent, independent of prior seasoning and entrusted-goods requests.
Admit the nine named Kāśikā bases as given and deny arbitrary unlisted perfume synonym substitution at this gate.
Retain the three additional Vasu list members under that explicitly broader named policy.
Admit both kiśara and kisara outputs on their positive source authority without duplicating the matched sale query.
Select the named narada output under its positive authority, preserving the niradika display as an Open comparison.
Select the uk-final ka output on guggulu and Vasu's haridru, with u retained and owner distinct.
Select ṣṭhan with its 4.1.41 feminine in the named class.
Write both śalālu outcomes under their own suffixes, with the graded arm limited to ṭhak.
Preserve the distinct ṅīṣ and ṅīp entries for the shared feminine outcome structure.
Credit the written accent outcomes at their own addressed masculine and feminine positions. Accent never creates additional segmental readings in this stage.
Permit the named scent bearer in the printed Padamañjarī explanation under the same merchandising guard.
Preserve the material-offering and other possession relation independently of these merchandise readings.
